event.whyItMatters: The co-located fairs place the exact suppliers a city needs — IoT connectivity, sensor hardware, urban platforms, building automation, mobility and waste/logistics integrators — in one venue, while CityAir brings the missing layer: a documented, comparable assessment of whether a city can actually use that technology, plus an innovation exchange that states what a deployment requires, risks and what to monitor.

cooperationModels.title: 1 · City pilot with a documented evidence trail
cooperationModels.forUs: The company provides sensors, connectivity or a platform for one district; CityAir provides the 12-domain readiness baseline, the evidence-confidence framework, the public dashboard text and the impact indicators. We publish what worked and what did not.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: The pilot is written up in the AQMx style: city context, method, data, results, limits — a candidate case study for the global exchange (subject to AQMx acceptance).
cooperationModels.ask: One pilot city, 3–6 sensors, 6 months, one agreed indicator set
cooperationModels.give: Independent assessment, transparent publication, no hidden endorsement

cooperationModels.title: 2 · Data and interoperability
cooperationModels.forUs: Their operational data (traffic counts, waste routes, building energy, gas detection) is mapped into CityAir's twelve domains so the assessment can cite real evidence instead of self-declared answers.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: Data dictionaries and metadata templates aligned with the exchange so other cities can reuse the same interface.
cooperationModels.ask: A documented data schema + a named data owner + an update cycle
cooperationModels.give: A public evidence register entry with provenance and quality notes

cooperationModels.title: 3 · Co-authored innovation brief
cooperationModels.forUs: The company submits a solution; CityAir co-authors the brief in the library template: problem, required capacity, required data, delivery steps, risks, adaptation notes, monitoring indicators.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: The brief becomes a reusable implementation record that cities anywhere can compare against their own readiness band.
cooperationModels.ask: One product, one honest limitation statement, one reference deployment
cooperationModels.give: Publication with full attribution and a link to the company

cooperationModels.title: 4 · Sponsorship with a firewall
cooperationModels.forUs: A company can fund an assessment cycle, a methane-screening study or a workshop series. Sponsors never set scores, never edit findings and are named as funders only.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: Sponsorship of knowledge products (sectoral guidance updates, translation, data hosting) with the same conflict-of-interest rules.
cooperationModels.ask: Funding with a written conflict-of-interest clause
cooperationModels.give: Public acknowledgement, no influence over results or rankings

cooperationModels.title: 5 · Capacity building and training
cooperationModels.forUs: Joint webinars and municipal workshops in Turkish, English and Persian on reading evidence quality, procurement of monitoring and communicating air-quality risk.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: Session materials contributed back to the exchange library so other cities and providers can reuse them.
cooperationModels.ask: Two experts and a venue or a webinar slot
cooperationModels.give: Trilingual materials, recorded sessions, a certificate of participation for municipal staff

cooperationModels.title: 6 · Independent evaluation partnership
cooperationModels.forUs: Before-and-after indicator tracking on a deployed system, with baseline, method and uncertainty stated in public.
cooperationModels.forAqmx: Evaluation reports that follow a comparable structure, so results from different cities and vendors can be read side by side.
cooperationModels.ask: Access to the deployment's operational data and permission to publish
cooperationModels.give: Third-party evaluation with a stated method — the strongest sales argument a vendor can hold

companies.name: Mavili Elektronik
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Fire and gas detection systems for buildings and industry — detector networks, control panels, alarm integration.
companies.aqAngle: Gas detection is the industrial sibling of ambient air monitoring: same sensor engineering, calibration discipline and alarm logic. Their installers already maintain sensor fleets in Istanbul.
companies.withCityAir: Pilot: extend an existing industrial gas-detection network with an ambient PM₂.₅/NO₂ layer; CityAir supplies the assessment baseline, calibration documentation standards and the public dashboard wording.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute a sectoral contribution on industrial gas-safety data as an evidence source in the emissions-inventory and decision-support domains.
companies.contact: Ask at their booth for the technical manager; mention CityAir's calibration-documentation standard

companies.name: AspenTech (Aspen Technology)
companies.presence: ISAF 2026 exhibitor (published testimonial on the ISAF site)
companies.whatTheyDo: Industrial process optimisation and asset-performance software for refineries, chemicals and energy.
companies.aqAngle: Their customers are the same plants that dominate industrial emission inventories. Emissions accounting that lands in the same database as production data is the fastest route to a verifiable inventory.
companies.withCityAir: Joint offer to industry: CityAir maps their facility emissions data into the city's inventory domain so the city assessment counts verified rather than estimated industry emissions.
companies.withAqmX: Propose an industrial-emissions data-interoperability note for the exchange: same schema, different cities.
companies.contact: Request the sustainability / ESG lead, not generic sales

companies.name: Ekingen Elektronik
companies.presence: ISAF 2026 exhibitor (published testimonial)
companies.whatTheyDo: Distributor of electronic security brands in Türkiye with a wide installer network.
companies.aqAngle: Distributors are the shortest path to hundreds of municipal and building installations — a distribution channel for low-cost indoor air-quality sensors with minimal extra sales effort.
companies.withCityAir: Bundle an IAQ module into their existing building installations; CityAir provides the health-domain questions and the reporting template for building managers.
companies.withAqmX: Feed building-level IAQ data into the health-impact and public-engagement domains as a documented evidence source.

companies.name: Art Sistem
companies.presence: ISAF 2026 exhibitor (published testimonial)
companies.whatTheyDo: Security and building technology integrator: access control, CCTV, building automation.
companies.aqAngle: Building automation platforms already carry CO₂, temperature and ventilation signals — the cheapest IAQ dataset in any city, usually thrown away.
companies.withCityAir: Integration brief: publish building IAQ indicators through CityAir's public-engagement domain; assessment question on ventilation and school/office exposure.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the 'buildings as sensors' approach as an innovation brief other cities can adapt.

companies.name: Reolink
companies.presence: Named in the ISAF 2026 exhibitor testimonial (Reolink participation)
companies.whatTheyDo: Smart visual technology: cameras, NVRs, solar-powered IoT units for homes and sites.
companies.aqAngle: Solar-powered outdoor edge devices are exactly the enclosure, power and connectivity package an off-grid air-quality node needs; open burning and waste-site detection is a camera-plus-sensor problem.
companies.withCityAir: Co-develop a waste-burning observation kit: camera evidence + PM spike correlation, feeding the open-waste-burning domain.
companies.withAqmX: Document the method as a replicable 'evidence for informal burning' case study.

companies.name: Nova Grup Mühendislik
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Engineering and installation contractor for technical systems in public and private projects.
companies.aqAngle: Municipal air-quality projects fail in installation and maintenance, not in procurement. Contractors own the maintenance contract that decides whether a sensor network survives its second winter.
companies.withCityAir: Add a maintenance-and-QA clause template to CityAir's procurement guidance, tested on their next municipal installation.
companies.withAqmX: Share the maintenance data (calibration intervals, failure rates, uptime) as an evidence-quality contribution.

companies.name: Yüksek Güvenlik
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: OSH services and equipment: worker protection, risk assessment, compliance.
companies.aqAngle: Workers in the informal sector (waste pickers, roadside vendors, construction) are the most exposed and the least measured group — an equity gap CityAir's health domain already flags.
companies.withCityAir: Street-level exposure and worker-protection pilot: personal exposure sampling plus CityAir's equity indicators.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the occupational-exposure angle to the health-impact guidance.

companies.name: Egesan Teknoloji Pazarlama
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Supplier of abrasive and industrial technology products since 1973.
companies.aqAngle: Industrial dust sources are a documented but rarely measured PM₁₀ contributor; suppliers see the processes that generate it.
companies.withCityAir: Dust-source inventory walkthrough: map their customer processes to the inventory domain and quantify what can be measured cheaply.
companies.withAqmX: Optional: a short note on industrial dust as a city inventory category.

companies.name: Sectec Security Technology
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Security systems supplier serving municipal and commercial projects.
companies.aqAngle: Their municipal relationships are the entry point; the ask is a joint proposal to a municipality that already buys security but has no air-quality line item.
companies.withCityAir: Joint municipal pitch: add an air-quality evidence line to an existing security/maintenance contract.
companies.withAqmX: Not applicable at this stage.

companies.name: Teknim
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Alarm-system manufacturer in Türkiye since 2003: fire detection, intruder alarms, integrated panels.
companies.aqAngle: Alarm infrastructure and municipal dispatch integration — the same channel that could carry a PM threshold alert to a school or a worksite.
companies.withCityAir: Alerting pilot: route CityAir's threshold alerts (for example PM₂.₅ above the 24-hour interim target) into their municipal dashboards.
companies.withAqmX: Contribution on alert delivery as part of the public-communication domain.

companies.name: İSTAÇ A.Ş. (İstanbul Metropolitan Municipality environmental company)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — İBB group company; verify attendance at the municipal pavilions
companies.whatTheyDo: İstanbul's waste management, landfill gas, transfer stations and disposal operations.
companies.aqAngle: Landfill methane and open burning are two of the twelve CityAir domains and the hardest for any city to evidence. İSTAÇ holds the operational data.
companies.withCityAir: Istanbul readiness assessment with real waste data; landfill-methane screening brief applied to one site; waste-burning reporting workflow with CityAir's Telegram bot for field crews.
companies.withAqmX: Case study: how a megacity evidences methane and waste burning — directly useful to the exchange's waste and methane themes.
companies.contact: Environmental management department; ask for the landfill-gas and reporting units separately

companies.name: İBB — Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (Smart City Directorate)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — municipalities are typically visitors or hosts at the venue
companies.whatTheyDo: City authority: environment, transport, waste, health and digital services.
companies.aqAngle: Istanbul is already in the CityAir city library as an illustrative profile; a real assessment would replace the synthetic score with documented evidence — the most valuable single upgrade the platform can get.
companies.withCityAir: Official 12-domain assessment of Istanbul, municipal workshop, and a public dashboard template they can host themselves.
companies.withAqmX: City-authored case study and a peer-review partner for the exchange's methodology discussions.
companies.contact: Smart City / Environment department; city delegations often meet at the fair's conference programme

companies.name: HAVELSAN
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — verify at the venue; HAVELSAN exhibits at Turkish smart-city events regularly
companies.whatTheyDo: Command-and-control and smart-city platforms, urban digital twin and data integration for municipalities.
companies.aqAngle: A city platform without an air-quality layer shows traffic but not exposure. Their dashboard is the ideal host for CityAir's domain scores and live readings.
companies.withCityAir: Embed the CityAir assessment widget and API into their municipal dashboard; joint tender for a pilot city.
companies.withAqmX: Joint session proposal on interoperable air-quality layers inside urban platforms.

companies.name: Netaş
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Systems integration, network infrastructure and IoT solutions for public authorities.
companies.aqAngle: Integration and maintenance contracts are what keep a sensor network alive; their service organisation covers most Turkish provinces.
companies.withCityAir: Service-level agreement template for air-quality networks; joint municipal bid.
companies.withAqmX: Contribution on uptime and data quality reporting as standard practice.

companies.name: Türk Telekom · Turkcell · Vodafone Business
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — mobile operators exhibit at the co-located MOBISAD IMEX fair
companies.whatTheyDo: National mobile networks, NB-IoT / LTE-M connectivity, IoT platforms and cloud services.
companies.aqAngle: Every low-cost sensor node needs a SIM, a data plan and an uplink that survives a power cut. Connectivity is the single largest recurring cost in a city sensor programme.
companies.withCityAir: Sponsored connectivity for a pilot network (for example 20 nodes, 12 months) plus data-plan templates so other cities can budget accurately.
companies.withAqmX: Publish a costed connectivity guideline for city sensor programmes in the exchange library.

companies.name: Arvento
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Vehicle tracking and fleet telematics, widely deployed in Turkish municipalities and logistics.
companies.aqAngle: Traffic emission inventories usually rely on modelled traffic counts. Fleet telematics gives measured movement of the vehicles that pollute most.
companies.withCityAir: Traffic-domain pilot: derive activity data for the emissions inventory from fleet traces, with privacy protection built in.
companies.withAqmX: Method note: telematics-derived traffic activity as an inventory input.

companies.name: Netcad
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Geographic information systems and urban data platforms used by many Turkish municipalities.
companies.aqAngle: Exposure is a map problem: population, schools, hospitals, industry and monitoring sites must share one geometry. Most cities have the layers but not the overlay.
companies.withCityAir: Exposure-mapping workshop: CityAir supplies the indicator definitions, Netcad supplies the geometry.
companies.withAqmX: Share the exposure-layer schema so other cities can reuse it.

companies.name: Evreka
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — Turkish waste-tech scale-up
companies.whatTheyDo: Software platform for waste collection fleets, routes, containers and reporting.
companies.aqAngle: Open burning and landfill fires are visible in collection data: missed pickups, overflowing containers and route gaps correlate with burning incidents.
companies.withCityAir: Pilot: correlate collection anomalies with CityAir's burning reports and PM spikes; publish a joint indicator set.
companies.withAqmX: Innovation brief: 'collection data as an open-burning early-warning signal'.

companies.name: Sensgreen
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Indoor air-quality monitoring and building analytics, deployed in offices, schools and public buildings.
companies.aqAngle: Indoor and outdoor data are rarely joined, so cities cannot show whether a ventilation measure actually protected children in classrooms.
companies.withCityAir: School pilot: pair indoor sensors with the nearest outdoor station and CityAir's health-domain indicators; publish the before/after.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the indoor–outdoor pairing method to the health-impact guidance.

companies.name: ASELSAN
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Defence electronics, sensor systems, imaging and communication technologies.
companies.aqAngle: Reference-grade photometers and optical particle sensors are a sensor-engineering problem; Türkiye imports most of this equipment. Local calibration capability is the bottleneck for credible low-cost networks.
companies.withCityAir: Co-designed sensor programme with a documented calibration protocol against a reference station — CityAir supplies the QA/QC rubric and publishes the comparison.
companies.withAqmX: Method contribution on low-cost sensor validation in the exchange.

companies.name: Mikrodev
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Turkish IoT hardware and telemetry devices for industrial and municipal monitoring.
companies.aqAngle: Hardware, enclosures and telemetry are commodity items; local manufacturing shortens repair cycles and lowers the cost of a city network.
companies.withCityAir: Costed hardware BOM for a 20-node network, published openly in CityAir's resources so every city can compare prices.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the open BOM to the exchange as a practical procurement aid.

companies.name: Karsan · Otokar · Bozankaya · Togg
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — mobility suppliers attend the Smartex transport track
companies.whatTheyDo: Bus and vehicle manufacturers: electric buses, e-mobility, charging infrastructure.
companies.aqAngle: Fleet electrification is the biggest single NO₂ lever in most Turkish cities, and it is measurable at depot level.
companies.withCityAir: Indicator partnership: track depot-level NO₂ and exposure reduction from e-bus deployment using CityAir's transport indicators.
companies.withAqmX: Case study: measured (not modelled) bus-fleet electrification impact.

companies.name: Enerjisa · Zorlu Enerji
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: Electricity distribution and generation, energy services and efficiency programmes.
companies.aqAngle: Household solid-fuel heating is the dominant winter PM source in Balkan and Anatolian cities; the heating transition is an energy-sector programme, not an environmental one.
companies.withCityAir: Heating-replacement evidence pack: join subsidy data with winter PM trends and CityAir's household-energy domain questions.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the heating-transition method to the sectoral guidance.

companies.name: Daikin Türkiye · Bosch Termoteknik · Vaillant Türkiye
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — smart-building halls host HVAC brands
companies.whatTheyDo: Heat pumps, boilers, ventilation and climate systems for residential and public buildings.
companies.aqAngle: Every heat-pump or ventilation upgrade changes both indoor exposure and outdoor emissions; almost none of it is documented for city planning.
companies.withCityAir: Public-building retrofit pilot with before/after indicators (energy, indoor PM/CO₂, outdoor contribution).
companies.withAqmX: Adaptation brief: retrofits as a co-benefit measure for both the household-energy and health domains.

companies.name: Urban platform vendors in the smart-city hall (IBM · Siemens · Cisco · local integrators)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — walk the smart-city hall and note who shows an environment module
companies.whatTheyDo: City operating systems, dashboards, digital twins, data-marketplace products.
companies.aqAngle: Platforms promise integration but usually display whatever data a city already had. Air quality is the classic missing module because it needs domain expertise, not only software.
companies.withCityAir: Module partnership: CityAir provides the air-quality and waste domain logic, assessment and knowledge base; the platform provides hosting, identity and municipal distribution.
companies.withAqmX: Propose a common air-quality module specification so cities can compare platform offers.
companies.contact: Smart city portfolio lead at each stand

companies.name: Start-up zone participants (Smartex start-up exhibition)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — scouting list built on site
companies.whatTheyDo: Early-stage teams in mobility, sensors, waste, energy and urban data.
companies.aqAngle: Start-ups can supply the missing measurement in a district for a few thousand euros, but rarely have a way to prove it changed anything.
companies.withCityAir: Offer the route to credibility: a CityAir innovation brief, an assessment-based baseline and a published pilot report in exchange for open data.
companies.withAqmX: Channel for their pilots to reach other cities, with the honesty template attached.
companies.contact: Scout 10 stands, collect 10 cards, log them in the tracker below

companies.name: Marmara Municipalities Union & municipal pavilions
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — municipal associations participate in Turkish smart-city events
companies.whatTheyDo: Network of municipalities around the Marmara region, training and cooperation programmes for local governments.
companies.aqAngle: One agreement with a municipal network distributes the readiness assessment to dozens of cities at once — the highest-leverage partnership available.
companies.withCityAir: Regional programme: train municipal staff, run assessments for member cities, publish a regional readiness map.
companies.withAqmX: Regional case study plus a pipeline of cities for the exchange.

companies.name: Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change (ÇŞB)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — national authorities attend the conference programme
companies.whatTheyDo: National air-quality law, monitoring network, permits, climate policy.
companies.aqAngle: CityAir's legal-domain questions must match national obligations; the ministry holds the authoritative monitoring network and the permits register.
companies.withCityAir: Alignment review: check the twelve domains against Turkish regulation and the national network so assessments are legally literate.
companies.withAqmX: Contribute the national regulatory mapping as a reusable template for other countries.

companies.name: TÜBİTAK MAM (Climate & Environment) · İTÜ · Boğaziçi · METU
companies.presence: Ecosystem target
companies.whatTheyDo: National research institutes and universities working on air quality, modelling, source apportionment and environmental engineering.
companies.aqAngle: Source apportionment and inventory QA are the two domains cities most often fail; the scientific capability already exists in Türkiye.
companies.withCityAir: Scientific advisory board: review the scoring weights and confidence model, co-author one domain guidance, supervise one student project per year.
companies.withAqmX: Peer review of method changes; co-publication of the corrected framework.

companies.name: International sensor vendors (Airly · AQMesh/Enviro Technology · Clarity · PurpleAir distributors)
companies.presence: Ecosystem target — approach their Turkish distributors and the foreign pavilions
companies.whatTheyDo: Low-cost and mid-cost air-quality sensor networks, calibration services and cloud platforms.
companies.aqAngle: Their hardware is proven; what is missing is an independent, comparable statement of what it achieved in a city — the exact product CityAir's evaluation model produces.
companies.withCityAir: Pilot evaluation: install, run six months, compare against a reference station, publish uptime, drift and data-quality results in a CityAir brief.
companies.withAqmX: Validation results go into the exchange so municipalities can compare vendors on measured performance, not marketing.

companies.name: Industry media present at the fair (Sanayi Haber Ajansı · Savunma Gazetesi · sector press)
companies.presence: Listed in the current ISAF exhibitor directory
companies.whatTheyDo: Trade press and news agencies covering the fair and the security/industrial sectors.
companies.aqAngle: A cooperation call only becomes real when it is public; trade media is the cheapest way to reach municipal buyers during the fair.
companies.withCityAir: One-page press note: what CityAir offers cities and suppliers, plus an invitation to publish their pilot results.
companies.withAqmX: Announcement channel for new knowledge products and city case studies.

templates.label: Booth visit — 20-second opener (English)
templates.body: Hello — I am with CityAir (aqmx.atikova.com), an independent platform that scores how ready a city actually is to use air-quality technology, and publishes implementation briefs. We are not selling sensors; we are building the evidence layer that makes your deployments defensible. Two questions: (1) do you have a municipal reference deployment in Türkiye we could document together, and (2) would you fund a six-month independent evaluation with published results? Here is a one-page brief and my card.

templates.label: Stant ziyareti — 20 saniyelik giriş (Türkçe)
templates.body: Merhaba — ben CityAir'den (aqmx.atikova.com). Bağımsız bir platformuz: bir şehrin hava kalitesi teknolojisini gerçekten kullanmaya ne kadar hazır olduğunu puanlıyor ve uygulama brifleri yayımlıyoruz. Sensör satmıyoruz; yatırımınızı savunulabilir kılan kanıt katmanını kuruyoruz. İki soru: (1) Türkiye'de birlikte belgeleyebileceğimiz bir belediye referans kurulumunuz var mı, (2) altı aylık bağımsız bir değerlendirmeyi ve sonuçların yayımlanmasını finanse eder misiniz? Bir sayfalık özet ve kartvizitim burada.

templates.label: ملاقات در غرفه — شروع ۲۰ ثانیهای (فارسی)
templates.body: سلام — من از CityAir هستم (aqmx.atikova.com)، یک پلتفرم مستقل که میسنجد یک شهر تا چه اندازه برای استفاده واقعی از فناوری کیفیت هوا آماده است و بریفهای اجرایی منتشر میکند. ما سنسور نمیفروشیم؛ لایهی شواهدی را میسازیم که سرمایهگذاری شما را قابلدفاع میکند. دو پرسش: (۱) آیا یک پروژهی مرجع شهرداری در ترکیه دارید که بتوانیم مشترکاً مستند کنیم؟ (۲) آیا حاضرید یک ارزیابی مستقل ششماهه با انتشار نتایج را تأمین مالی کنید؟ این هم خلاصهی یکصفحهای و کارت من.

templates.body:

Dear [Name],

Thank you for the time at ISAF Smartex ([date], stand [no.]). As discussed, CityAir is an independent platform that assesses city readiness across twelve domains and publishes implementation briefs with stated risks and monitoring indicators.

What we propose: [model — city pilot / innovation brief / independent evaluation].
What we need from you: [one sensor set / data schema / funding / access for six months].
What we deliver: a public brief with method, limits and results, attributed to you.

Our rule is simple: no sponsor sets a score, and every limitation is published. That is what makes the result usable by a municipality.

Next step: 30 minutes next week to agree scope and timeline?

outreachChecklist: Before the hall: write the top five targets on paper, with the exact question you will ask each one.
Bring A5 one-pagers in EN and TR: what CityAir is, the six cooperation models, one example indicator.
Ask every vendor the same three questions: a named reference city, real uptime figures, and whether they will publish results.
Never argue about prices at the fair — ask for the person who owns the municipal account and the data.
Collect the data schema, not the brochure: how is their data structured, who owns it, how often is it updated?
Photograph the hall plan and note the stand number for every serious conversation.
Log every card in the tracker table the same evening, while the context is fresh (the tracker table is below).
Send the follow-up within 24 hours with one specific ask and one specific deliverable.
Mark the follow-up date in the calendar; a promise made at a fair and not followed within a week is dead.
